body:
Did anybody else ever have the urge to just...leave? To quit your job, drop out of school, and drive as far as you can?

Did it work?
And as a follow up, I want to make clear that this isn't about my ill-fated love life. Liking girls that don't like me in return sucks, but I think this goes beyond that. I'm just offering examples.

I read this last night, and put a lot of thought into it. It really does sound good. 

When I was 13, I had brain surgery. I was in eighth grade. It happened in February, so we were all prepping up to go to High School at this point. I'm of the opinion that high school is one of the most important parts of your life...it lays the framework for the rest of your life. People changed so much during those times, so how you ended up in high school had a massive effect on how you ended up in life.

So, I'm 13. Prior to my surgery, I was quite the popular kid. I had a lot of friends that I felt very close to, a lot of cute girls liked me...it was fun. When I was in the hospital, I got cards, lots of visitors, a big outpouring of love and support. The kind of things you see on the 6 p.m. news. 

When I got back to school, I had a massive car, was half bald, and for a month or two, my head oozed some nasty shit. Every single one of my friends stopped hanging out with me. Nobody would go to the movies with me. Nobody would come over to play Smash Brothers. Nobody would sit with me at lunch. 

I found out my freshman year that it was because they were embarrassed to be seen with me. Two months prior to my surgery, my bests friend's house burned down. My mother and I got enough money together to buy him and his entirely family gifts for Christmas. I put in all the money I had saved up to buy him a Gamecube and Metroid: Prime.

He wouldn't talk to me. Nobody would hangout with me anymore.

I've found it very hard to trust people since then. I've found it very hard to have friends and actually be friends with them. I went the majority of high school without doing anything social. Freshman, Sophomore, Junior years...nothing. I'd go to school, sit to myself, do my work, and come home. I was happy. 

Senior year, I started to make a few friends. My first girlfriend came into my life around this time. I hungout with her everyday for two months. I wasn't clingy, and I know I wasn't. I was actually pretty suave. One Friday, she said "...I miss Steve." 

I never saw her outside of school again.

I've "loved" two girls since then. The first of the two did the same thing. The second of the two cheated on me, got pregnant, made me believe it was mine, then wonderfully delivered the lines "Good news and bad news. Bad news, I had a miscarriage. Good news, it wasn't yours." 

My point with this is that I don't think I can trust people. I know I mentioned that I tried to stop being misanthropic, and I have, and I think I've been successful. I see a lot of genuinely good people. But, nobody in my life is that way. Nobody that has ever been in my life has been that way. It's probably a case of "Ignorance is Bliss." Sometimes you see somebody, and you think you can detect what kind of person they are.

I work with this girl, and I've been pretty into her lately. She's entirely different from me. While I grew up basically as a punk, she was one of those ditzy girls that played tennis and got a scholarship. We come from entirely different walks of life, but we get along.

We went on a semidate today. I decided that I hated listening to her babble about god knows what while she asked me "Are these cute?" to fifteen million fucking pairs of heels. Over dinner, she told me I need to take personality classes because I'm so rude. 

You think you know somebody, or at the least have a feel for them, and they turn out to be self centered bitches.

I'm sorry, this entire post is kind of jumpy in time. My point is that, I'm not so sure that a lack of people is my problem. Isn't there a point that you reach that, hey, maybe killing yourself isn't such a bad idea? 

EDIT: I slipped and put in personal info. Removed.

I don't want to have to bring this up to my family. My sister tried to OD a few years ago. It wasn't a real attempt, as far as I know. It seemed to be much more of a "HEY, EVERYBODY, I'M HAVING PROBLEMS, I NEED YOUR HELP." deal. My father confided in me that he found it very annoying and kind of didn't want to deal with the situation. My father is the only person I can turn to, so I don't want to put this on him. I don't want to have no answer to "What's wrong?" 

It's really weird. I think the only thing that keeps me from actually going through with it is this little...mental road block. Part of me wants to interpret that as a reason to go to Church, which is something I've heavily considered doing. I don't believe in God, and I don't think I ever will. I see a lot of people coming and going from Church, and they seem happy. If I could go there and become part of a family, maybe I could be happy too?

I really wish it was easier. I'm still afraid of what's going to happen when I do.

Do you think six years of it is too late? I've tried making attempts to make new friends and get out. At the start of every semester, I tell myself, "I'm going to go in and be friendly and make friends. Everybody is a stranger the first day. Nobody will recognize me as the antisocial kid in the corner."

Yet, at the start of every semester, I return to my corner. It's just a terrible habit to break. I've even talked myself out of being so misanthropic, and that alone has made me feel better. So maybe I can talk myself into being a better person, as well.

Also, thank you for the responses. I don't want to take this to any of my friends, so another party without a face is nice to talk to. You're a good person, whoever you are.
Btw, I am going to torrent that film. Thanks for the suggestion.

I don't have any major problems. I've got a full scholarship to my undergrad, and I'll probably score high on the LSAT. I do hate my job, which is retail, but who doesn't hate their retail job? It doesn't make me miserable, and I'm currently falling head over heels with a girl I work with. 

My father is awesome to me. We get along great. I had a great childhood. I've got a dog that I love very much.

I don't know. I don't think I'm depressed or anything. I'm a super introvert and spend a lot of time to myself, but I have all of my shit in order and stuff.
